commitResults.messageBody: Introduce TaskList as the owner of the in-memory task collection, including task addition, retrieval, removal, counting, and a read-only view for persistence.\n\nUpdate Alice to delegate collection operations to TaskList while retaining command handling and preserving all existing console output. This creates a focused domain abstraction that will support later Parser and Ui extractions without changing user-visible behavior.

Introduce Ui to own Alice's standard-input reading and all console rendering, including task confirmations, errors, task lists, and date-query results.\n\nUpdate Alice to coordinate commands through Ui while preserving the existing command behaviour and exact user-visible output. This narrows Alice's responsibility and prepares the remaining command interpretation logic for a later Parser extraction.

Introduce Parser to identify command words, create todo, deadline, and event tasks, validate task numbers, and parse date-query arguments.\n\nSimplify Alice so it coordinates parsed commands with TaskList, Storage, and Ui instead of directly performing input validation and date-time conversion. Existing command behaviour and output are preserved.

Add TaskList date-query operations that determine whether deadlines and events occur on a requested date.\n\nUpdate Ui to render the returned matching tasks without inspecting task subtypes. This keeps date-matching domain rules with the collection that owns the tasks while preserving current output and task numbering.

Move Alice classes from the default package into alice, alice.ui, alice.parser, alice.storage, alice.task, and alice.exception packages.\n\nAdd the package declarations and cross-package imports required by the new structure while keeping src/main/java as the source root. This separates application coordination, user interaction, parsing, persistence, task-domain classes, and exception handling without changing runtime behaviour.
Record in Alice that Codex was used to support the OOP class design.

commitResults.messageBody:
The Java sources use inconsistent import grouping, documentation punctuation, and local naming. This makes the code less consistent with the project standard.

Standardize imports, Javadoc wording, line wrapping, and variable names without changing application behavior. Add project skills and agent rules so future Java changes and Git commits follow the same conventions.

Users can now search task descriptions with find <keyword>. Matching is case-insensitive and keeps each task's original list number.

Reject empty keywords and report when no tasks match. Cover matching, no-match, and invalid-input cases with JUnit and UI tests.

The project lacks automated enforcement of the SE-EDU Java style standard, leaving formatting issues easy to miss.

Add the Checkstyle plugin and configuration, and format parser tests to comply with the configured rules.
Add a JavaFX chat interface with FXML layouts, message dialogs, and styling. Reuse Alice command handling so the GUI and console share the same behavior.

Command handling in Alice.getResponse mixes command selection with individual command implementations, resulting in mixed abstraction levels.

Introduce a Command enum to centralize supported command words, dispatch commands through a switch expression, and move longer command actions to focused methods.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for task model invariants
commitResults.messageBody: Task construction and task-list operations rely on valid task data and validated arguments.\nAdd assertions to detect violations during development.

Storage.parseTask combines token normalization, common-field validation,
subtype construction, date parsing, and status restoration. That makes the
persistence format difficult to read and change safely.

Extract one helper for each parsing responsibility so parseTask presents the
high-level sequence while retaining the existing validation messages and
storage behavior.

Date and keyword search responses each construct the same numbered task
list. Keeping two copies means output formatting can diverge when either
feature changes.

Extract the common formatting loop into a focused helper while preserving
each command's existing heading and empty-result response.

Command keywords are defined by the Command enum but also repeated as
strings in Alice and Parser. Those copies can drift, causing incorrect
argument extraction or inconsistent command handling.

Expose each enum's command word and use the enum at parser call sites.
Update parser tests to exercise the type-safe API.

Ui retains task-specific display methods even though command processing now
formats responses in Alice. The stale methods duplicate inactive behaviour and
make it harder to identify the active output path.

Remove the unused display methods and their imports while preserving the
console and graphical interface methods that are still called.

Parser embeds task delimiters, split limits, and the event-format error in
several parsing expressions. Those unexplained literals obscure the command
grammar and make changes easy to apply inconsistently.

Name the grammar elements once and reuse the shared event validation message
without changing accepted input or response text.

Mark, unmark, and delete each parse a one-based task number and convert it
to a zero-based list index. Repeating that setup hides the shared command
contract and risks inconsistent indexing in future changes.

Extract the conversion into one helper while retaining each command's
separate state validation and response behavior.

The console maintains its own goodbye message while Alice already supplies
the same response for the graphical interface. The command keyword is also
repeated separately in both interface paths.

Route console goodbye through Alice's response method and use Command.BYE in
both interfaces, leaving one active source for the keyword and response.

Each command parser removes its command word and trims the remaining input
before applying command-specific validation. Repeating that manipulation makes
the shared command structure harder to recognize and maintain.

Extract one helper for argument parsing so individual methods focus on their
own validation and task construction rules.

Storage.load exposes ArrayList even though callers only require the List
operations accepted by TaskList. The concrete return type couples callers to
the storage implementation without providing a needed capability.

Return List<Task> from the storage API while retaining the current internal
ArrayList implementation and loading behavior.

Alice supports todo, deadline, and event tasks, while a plain Task has no
concrete type for storage or display. Allowing direct construction permits an
object the application cannot persist as a valid task.

Make Task an abstract base class so the type system requires callers to use
one of the supported concrete task types.

Storage repeats the short task type codes when writing tasks and when reading
them back. Those literals define one format contract, but separate copies can
drift and make the format less self-explanatory.

Name each storage task type once and reuse the constants for serialization and
parsing without changing the saved-file format.

Storage writes and reads completion using the raw values 0 and 1 in
separate expressions. Those literals encode part of the file format but do
not reveal whether they represent completed or incomplete tasks.

Name both persisted status markers and use them throughout storage parsing and
serialization without changing the file format.

Date and keyword searches each traverse the task list, collect matches, and
preserve original order. Maintaining separate loops duplicates the collection
logic and makes future filtering changes harder to apply consistently.

Extract the ordered filtering operation while keeping each public method's
date or keyword matching rule explicit.

TaskList keeps its task collection in an ArrayList-typed field even though
all internal operations use the List contract. The concrete declaration couples
the class to an implementation detail it does not require.

Declare the field as List<Task> while retaining the current ArrayList
construction and behavior.

The previous change applies an interface-based declaration in TaskList,
but provides no practical improvement beyond the identical API-boundary
refactoring already made in Storage.

Revert the redundant field-type change so each iteration remains a
distinct, meaningful code-quality improvement.

The mark and unmark commands follow the same task lookup, status
validation, persistence, and response workflow, but previously maintain
two nearly identical implementations.

Centralize that shared workflow while retaining each command's distinct
status transition and user-facing wording. This reduces duplication and
keeps future changes to status handling consistent.

Date and keyword searches manually traverse the same ordered task list
to collect matching tasks. The collection workflow obscures the filtering
intent and duplicates traversal code.

Express both searches as ordered stream filters so each method directly
states its matching condition while preserving the existing results.
Use streams for task filtering

Master adds stream-based task filtering while this branch centralizes the
shared filtering workflow. Resolve the overlap by retaining the shared
method and implementing it with the stream pipeline.

This incorporates master without losing the code-quality improvement and
keeps date and keyword searches consistent.

Master replaces task-search collection loops with ordered stream filters,
while this branch adds precondition assertions to those search methods.

Resolve the overlap by retaining the assertion checks before the stream
pipelines, so the merged branch includes both sets of improvements.
Add assertions for task model invariants

Master adds task-model assertions and stream-based searches, while this
branch keeps the search workflow centralized in a shared helper.

Resolve the overlap by retaining the assertion checks and shared helper,
whose implementation uses the stream pipeline from master.
Branch a code quality

Scheduled tasks do not retain recurrence information or create future occurrences when completed.

Add recurrence commands, persistence, scheduling behavior, tests, and user documentation so deadlines and events can repeat safely.
Add recurring task support

Event output currently uses uppercase meridiem labels, while the
application's display convention and tests use lowercase labels.

Format event times with lowercase am and pm indicators so recurring
events render consistently.
